title: About this model
body: An interactive 3D atlas of the head and neck of an adult man and woman. The faces belong to two individual, idealised people created for this atlas: they are neither an average face nor a portrait of any real person.

Anatomy: 640+ structures from Z-Anatomy / BodyParts3D, warped with a smooth thin-plate deformation so that 11 standard skull measurements match published adult anthropometric means (references below).

Faces and skin: two people cast with Higgsfield, reconstructed in 3D from several views and aligned to the skull. The anatomy is re-fitted inside each face with a smooth deformation that keeps the cranial vault at the measurement targets.
Female head: a face of its own; the skull and organs follow published female cranial means and regional sex differences from CT studies (brow ridge, forehead, mastoid, larynx), re-fitted to the face.
Every fact shown was checked against its source by an independent verification pass.
simpl: The faces are narrower than the target means: cheekbone width −6% for the man and −3% for the woman, jaw width −7% and −6%. The cranial vault matches the targets within 2% (man) and 3.4% (woman).
Hair is part of the 3D face surface, not individual strands; in a section a gap between the skull and the hair is visible.
Neck and scalp follow the reference anatomy where no measurement data exist; neck circumference is not fitted.
Internal organs, vessels and nerves keep the shape of one reference body, scaled with the skull; small branches are schematic.
Some Kazakh anatomical terms have no approved equivalent yet; about 175 terms are marked for review by a Kazakh-speaking anatomist.
The inner-ear model (cochlea, vestibule) is omitted because its licence does not permit this use.
